Subject: POC capacity planning - Acme AI (trial) - next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — nice to dig into the evaluation plan. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the success criteria and propose next steps so we can lock the capacity plan for the upcoming trial.

Success criteria (as I heard it):
- End-to-end latency <= 600ms p95 for single-turn generation at 512 tokens
- Throughput to support up to 40 concurrent inference sessions at peak
- No more than 2% error rate (timeouts / 5xx) during the 2-week trial
- Sample quality parity vs. your internal baseline (you'll provide eval prompt set)

Evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize model & test prompts, agree on test harness and metrics
- Week 1: run initial scale test (synthetic load) to validate capacity assumptions
- Week 2: seeded production traffic with real requests, monitor SLOs and cost metrics

Owners / asks:
- Acme: provide eval prompts and representative traffic pattern (qps, session length) — Alex / Priya
- Redwood: provide POC capacity plan (reserved GPUs + autoscale policy) and a test URL + metrics dashboard — Marissa + Dylan

Questions we still need to confirm:
1) Target model & variant for the trial (FP16 / 8-bit quantized?)
2) Expected burst behavior (how often do you see spikes above peak?)
3) Any regulatory constraints for data retention or VPC-only connectivity

If that summary looks right, I'll loop in Vivek to propose the GPU reservation and autoscale configuration. I can share a short capacity plan doc for your review by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that captures it well. Quick answers from our side:

- Model: We'll start with "acme/open-13b" (FP16) for quality parity. If needed we'll test an 8-bit quantized build later in the trial.
- Traffic: Typical baseline is ~15 concurrent sessions, but bursts up to ~60 concurrents happen during product demos (lasting ~2-3 minutes). Spikes occur a few times per day.
- Prompts / eval set: Priya will share the 120 test prompts and a short CSV with request size distribution by EOD tomorrow.
- Data handling: PII is rare for the test data; standard access control + logs are fine. We can provide a signed NDA if needed.

Questions for you:
1) For the bursts to 60 concurrents, do you recommend reserved capacity or autoscale with burst buffer?
2) What latency degradation should we expect under burst vs. reserved pool?

Appreciate Vivek's input on the infra side — cc'ing him here.

Thanks,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@acme.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T18:00:00Z
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning - Acme AI (trial) - next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks for the details. Quick capacity proposal based on the targets (p95 <= 600ms, peaks ~60 concurrents):

Summary (high level):
- Reserved pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (for the 13B FP16 model) dedicated to the trial. This covers baseline concurrency (15) with headroom for steady-state load and provides stable latency.
- Autoscale policy: configure warm autoscale group that can add up to 4 additional GPUs for burst capacity (total max 8). Scaling trigger based on queue length and avg token-latency rising above target; scale-in after sustained healthy metrics for 5 minutes.
- Burst buffer: short-lived burst allowance (30-90s) where requests queue for up to 2 seconds before an additional GPU spins up — this keeps cost down while smoothing brief spikes. For your demo spikes (~2-3 min) the autoscaler will typically add 2-3 GPUs within 45-60s.
- Expected latency: under reserved-only (4 GPUs) we expect to meet p95 <=600ms for baseline and moderate load; under burst when extra GPUs are provisioning you may see p95 degrade to ~900-1200ms briefly until new workers are ready. With the warm autoscale and burst buffer configured as above, most 2-3 minute spikes will have partial headroom from the buffer and then stabilize once autoscale completes.
- Cost note: reserved pool + small warm buffer reduces per-token cost vs. fully provisioned max capacity. We'll include an estimated cost delta in the attached capacity plan.

Operational items / next steps:
1) We'll provision the 4 reserved GPUs for trial start date (proposed: 2026-09-08).
2) Set autoscale policy with max 8 GPUs and warm buffer as described.
3) Provide a test endpoint and Grafana dashboard (token-level latency, queue length, GPU utilization) — Dylan to own dashboards.
4) Run a synthetic scale test (Week 1) to validate spikes to 60 concurrents; we'll capture telemetry and adjust scaling thresholds.

Attachment: acme_poc_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (contains sizing math, estimated cost, scaling thresholds, and runbook).

Let me know if you want tighter p95 guarantees — we can increase reserved GPUs or warm buffer at an incremental cost.

-Vivek
Head of Infra — Redwood Inference
